paper_sections.title: Perceptual and categorical decision making: goal-relevant representation of two domains at different levels of abstraction.
Drift Diffusion Model and Domain Interaction
Parametric representation of stimulus features within the brain.
FPN dynamics as a function of feature salience.
FPN Representation of Multiple Sources of Information
Frontal-Parietal Dissociation and Cognitive Control Within FPN

description.value: The study examined how perceptual salience and categorical salience contribute to perceptual categorization and how these information domains are represented in frontoparietal brain networks.

design.value: Ten subjects performed a visual random-dot motion categorization task during four fMRI sessions; perceptual salience was varied by motion coherence and categorical salience by motion direction relative to an oblique category boundary.

source_definition.value: Perceptual salience was altered by changing dot-motion coherence: salience decreased as motion coherence decreased.
Categorical salience was manipulated by varying the direction of motion of the dots: salience decreased as the coherently moving dots moved closer to the boundary line.
Subject accuracies in the 20 stimulus combinations were rank-ordered into four separate bins.

description.value: Ten subjects participated; one subject was excluded because of a high percentage of aborted trials, leaving nine subjects for the behavioral and imaging analyses.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist

exclusion_criteria.value: responded outside the response window in >20% of trials within each run in two scanner sessions

medical_condition.value: normal neural anatomy; normal or corrected-to-normal vision

task_description.value: Subjects viewed a variable proportion of coherently moving dots on a background of randomly moving dots and categorized the direction of motion as either leftward or rightward of an oblique boundary.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report their choice via a button press as quickly and accurately as possible, using the index or middle finger of their right hand.

stimuli.value: Random dot kinematogram; dots moved in 1 of 16 different directions, with variable motion coherence and an oblique category boundary inclined at either 45° or 135° from the horizontal.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr. Brain Imaging Center at the University of California, Berkeley

description.value: Functional images consisted of 32 slices acquired with a single-shot gradient echoplanar imaging protocol in a contiguous order. Images were collected with a 12-channel phased-array coil.

definition.value: Tests of linear trends were carried out for each voxel using the distance from category boundary vector transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1 and then applied to the estimated β-coefficients.

interpretations.value: Frontal regions strongly differentiated categorical salience, while parietal activity varied strongly with categorical information.

definition.value: Tests of linear trends were carried out for each voxel using the coherence vector transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1 and then applied to the estimated β-coefficients.

interpretations.value: Perceptual information produced a predominantly positive parametric effect within frontoparietal network nodes.

definition.value: A three-factor ANOVA was performed with motion coherence and distance from category boundary comprising the fixed factors and subjects the random factor; the reported effect was their interaction.

interpretations.value: The interaction between perceptual and categorical salience activated similar frontoparietal brain networks.

name.value: Brain areas showing interaction effects after low-salience conditions were excluded

definition.value: The ANOVA was repeated after excluding all 0% motion coherence and 0° category distance conditions; the reported effect was the interaction between the two domains.

interpretations.value: A significant interaction between the two domains remained evident in many regions within the frontoparietal network even when zero-salience conditions were not included.

definition.value: Accuracies in the 20 unique stimulus combinations were rank-ordered into four bins, averaged within each bin, transformed to a zero-mean vector with sum of squares equal to 1, and applied as parametric weights to the stimulus regressors.

interpretations.value: The same frontoparietal nodes demonstrating an interaction between stimulus domains also showed a negative parametric effect of accuracy, underscoring the relevance of these interactions to behavior.

name.value: Parametric representation of categorical salience at each level of perceptual salience

role.value: parametric predictor at each value of motion coherence

definition.value: Parametric effects of categorical salience were assessed at each value of perceptual salience.

interpretations.value: At the lowest perceptual salience there was minimal parametric activity in the frontoparietal network; as motion coherence increased, the parametric effect of categorical salience grew more negative.

name.value: Parametric representation of perceptual salience at each level of categorical salience

role.value: parametric predictor at each value of distance from category boundary

definition.value: Parametric effects of perceptual salience were assessed at each value of categorical salience.

interpretations.value: At the lowest categorical salience, parietal but not frontal cortex showed a robust positive parametric effect as a function of perceptual salience; at high salience in either domain, the network showed negative parametric modulation as a function of salience in the other domain.

name.value: Contrast of parametric category activity at 100% vs. 0% coherence

role.value: parametric effect contrasted across perceptual salience levels

definition.value: Contrast of parametric category activity at 100% vs. 0% coherence.

interpretations.value: All nodes of the frontoparietal network demonstrated changes in parametric activity along the salience spectrum.

name.value: Contrast of parametric motion coherence activity at 90° vs. 0° distance from category boundary

role.value: parametric effect contrasted across categorical salience levels

definition.value: Contrast of parametric motion coherence activity at 90° vs. 0° distance from category boundary.

interpretations.value: All nodes of the frontoparietal network demonstrated changes in parametric activity along the salience spectrum in both domains.

name.value: Contrast of parametric motion coherence activity at 0° from category boundary with parametric category activity at 0% motion coherence

definition.value: Contrast of parametric motion coherence activity at 0° from category boundary with parametric category activity at 0% motion coherence.

interpretations.value: At low salience, the contrast map was similar to the map showing parametric effects of coherence, highlighting that frontoparietal activity was limited to parietal regions and driven primarily by perceptual information.

name.value: Contrast of parametric category activity at 100% coherence with parametric motion coherence activity at 90° from category boundary

definition.value: Contrast of parametric category activity at 100% coherence with parametric motion coherence activity at 90° from category boundary.

interpretations.value: At high salience, all nodes in the frontoparietal network exhibited parametric activity during categorization, indicating that both features contributed to the choice.
